verdict.rationale: Pomelo documents that Reversal and Refund transactions are pushed to the developer through the Adjustments endpoint, alongside its ability to authorize and adjust transactions outside its core, so some post-auth events do reach the developer programmatically. Clearings, chargeback notifications and stable transaction identifiers for reconciliation are not evidenced; chargebacks appear only as dispute escalation, not as delivered events. Missing for 10: clearing/settlement event delivery, chargeback events delivered as webhooks, documented stable transaction identifiers linking auth to post-auth events, payload/retry details, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, post-auth events are as programmatic as auth — clearings, refunds, reversals, and chargebacks arrive as webhooks with stable transaction identifiers, so my own ledger never drifts

citations.quote: Recibirás las transacciones de tipo Reversal y Refund a través del endpoint de Ajustes.
Autorizar y ajustar transacciones sin usar nuestro Core de crédito o Autorizador.
